title: Study protocol – A Randomized controlled trial of efficacy of metronome on quality of chest compressions during simulated cardiopulmonary resuscitation among novice nurses
author: Harikrishnan, Solayappan, et al.

steps.title: Recruit and allocate participants
steps.instruction: Enroll 160 novice nurses and randomly assign 80 to the intervention group and 80 to the control group.

steps.title: Set up simulation equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare a Q‑CPR manikin with its built‑in feedback system; ensure a metronome device is available and can be set to 110 compressions per minute.

steps.title: Perform pre‑test CPR session
steps.instruction: Have each participant complete a 2‑minute compression‑only CPR trial on the manikin without any metronome guidance.

steps.title: Rest interval between tests
steps.instruction: Allow a 20‑minute rest period for each participant to prevent fatigue before the next trial.

steps.title: Perform post‑test CPR sessions
steps.instruction: Conduct a second 2‑minute compression‑only CPR trial for each participant according to group assignment.

substeps.instruction: Intervention group: use the metronome set at 110 cpm during the trial.
Control group: perform the trial under standard conditions without metronome assistance.

steps.title: Record CPR performance metrics
steps.instruction: Capture compression rate, depth, recoil, and overall performance from the manikin’s feedback system for both pre‑ and post‑test trials.

steps.title: Statistical data analysis
steps.instruction: Import the collected data into SPSS version 22; compute descriptive statistics (frequency, percentage, mean, SD); conduct repeated‑measures ANOVA for within‑ and between‑group comparisons; perform chi‑square test for post‑test categorical outcomes; run paired t‑tests for pre‑ vs post‑test within each group and independent t‑tests for between‑group post‑test differences; consider results significant at p < 0.05.
